fullPassage: A person, let's call him Opt (for optimist), never goes to the doctor and feels healthy. Opt will likely have nothing to worry about until later in life—perhaps until it is too late. Yet, until that time, Opt can claim that he is healthy and that he has nothing to worry about. A friend of his, Caut (for cautious), is more proactive. He regularly visits the doctor from an early age, and, as soon as he realizes that his blood pressure is above the normal range, he starts losing weight and exercising more than before. Caut starts feeling awkward because he cannot eat and drink as much as his friend Opt, and he has to walk to work in order to exercise. Opt even makes fun of him, calling him an imaginary patient. Should Caut feel embarrassed? No! Caut is doing what he can to lead a better life in the long term; he is self-correcting his life habits. Opt has left things to chance and does not worry if he does harm to his body. Science is like Caut, not Opt: it is a self-correcting enterprise that aims for the best possible condition. It's not embarrassed to correct itself, unlike other enterprises that are either unaware of their problems or prefer to live in eternal ignorance. This self-awareness and self-correcting aspect of science provides a good reason to trust it despite its failings. As it was nicely put recently: The discovery that an experiment does not replicate is not a lack of success but an opportunity. Many of the current concerns about reproducibility represent the dynamic, iterative nature of the process of discovery where discordant results are essential to producing more integrated accounts and (eventually) translation. A failure to reproduce is only the first step in scientific inquiry. In many ways, how science responds to these failures is what determines whether it succeeds.

[조건] (1) Opt, and, as, as, cannot, drink, eat, friend, he, his, much를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 11단어로 쓸 것
(영어로)

det.korean: 주어 he + 'cannot + 동사원형'으로 '~할 수 없다'를 만들어요. eat and drink(먹고 마시다)를 쓰고, '~만큼'은 'as much as'로 연결한 뒤 his friend Opt(그의 친구 Opt)로 마무리해요.
det.analysis:
주어(he) → cannot + 동사원형(eat and drink) → 원급 비교 'as much as'(~만큼 많이) → 비교 대상(his friend Opt) 순서예요.

본문: 'he cannot eat and drink as much as his friend Opt'

he + cannot + eat + and + drink + as + much + as + his + friend + Opt = 11단어. 동사 두 개를 and로 병렬 연결하고, 양을 비교하므로 much(셀 수 없는 양)를 써요.
det.tip: as much as = ~만큼 (많이). 양을 비교할 땐 much. eat and drink처럼 동사는 and로 병렬

accept: he cannot eat and drink as much as his friend Opt

questions.passage: A person, let's call him Opt (for optimist), never goes to the doctor and feels healthy. Opt will likely have nothing to worry about until later in life—perhaps until it is too late. Yet, until that time, Opt can claim that he is healthy and that he has nothing to worry about. A friend of his, Caut (for cautious), is more proactive. He regularly visits the doctor from an early age, and, as soon as he realizes that his blood pressure is above the normal range, he starts losing weight and exercising more than before. Caut starts feeling awkward because he cannot eat and drink as much as his friend Opt, and he has to walk to work in order to exercise. Opt even makes fun of him, calling him an imaginary patient. Should Caut feel embarrassed? No! Caut is doing what he can to lead a better life in the long term; he is self-correcting his life habits. Opt has left things to chance and does not worry if he does harm to his body. Science is like Caut, not Opt: __________. It's not embarrassed to correct itself, unlike other enterprises that are either unaware of their problems or prefer to live in eternal ignorance. This self-awareness and self-correcting aspect of science provides a good reason to trust it despite its failings. As it was nicely put recently: The discovery that an experiment does not replicate is not a lack of success but an opportunity. Many of the current concerns about reproducibility represent the dynamic, iterative nature of the process of discovery where discordant results are essential to producing more integrated accounts and (eventually) translation. A failure to reproduce is only the first step in scientific inquiry. In many ways, how science responds to these failures is what determines whether it succeeds.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 [보기]의 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.
그것은 최상의 가능한 상태를 지향하는 자기수정적 활동이다.
[보기] a, aims, best, condition, enterprise, for, is, it, possible, self-correcting, that, the
(12단어, 영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 주어 it + be동사 is + 보어(a self-correcting enterprise)를 놓고, 그 enterprise를 꾸미는 주격 관계대명사 that + aims for(~을 지향하다)로 이어요. 마지막에 the best possible condition(최상의 가능한 상태)을 붙여요.
det.analysis:
주어(it) → be동사(is) → 보어 명사구(a self-correcting enterprise) → 주격 관계대명사(that) → 동사구(aims for) → 목적어(the best possible condition) 순서예요.

본문: 'it is a self-correcting enterprise that aims for the best possible condition'

it+is+a+self-correcting+enterprise+that+aims+for+the+best+possible+condition = 12단어. 선행사 enterprise가 단수라 관계사절 동사는 aims(-s)예요.
det.tip: 명사(enterprise)를 뒤에서 꾸밀 땐 주격 관계대명사 that + 동사. aim for = ~을 지향하다

questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 [조건]을 사용하여 문장을 완성하시오.
그는 자신의 생활 습관을 스스로 고쳐 나가고 있다.
[조건] (1) habits, he, his, is, life, self-correcting를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 6단어로 쓸 것
(영어로)

det.korean: 주어 he + be동사 is + 현재분사 self-correcting으로 현재진행형(~하고 있다)을 만들고, 목적어 his life habits(자신의 생활 습관)를 이어요.
det.analysis:
주어(he) → be동사(is) → 현재분사(self-correcting) = 현재진행형 '~하고 있다' → 목적어(his life habits) 순서예요.

본문: 'he is self-correcting his life habits'

he + is + self-correcting + his + life + habits = 6단어. be동사 + V-ing로 '지금 ~하는 중'을 나타내요.
det.tip: be동사 + V-ing = 현재진행형(~하고 있다). his life habits = 자신의 생활 습관
